purpose: Turn the Core5 5+5 source-grounded briefs into consistent anime-production-style setting boards that communicate ordinary systems, population diversity and reusable visual evidence rather than ten unrelated mood illustrations.

environment.purpose: Show how ordinary Reality-era infrastructure is used, carried, repaired, waited for, navigated and recorded.

requiredPanels.role: One readable ordinary environment view with multiple established systems visible in use; not a cinematic key art shot.
Small comparative panels for communication, transport/navigation, shopping/availability, repair/replacement and privacy/records.
Close references for ordinary carried objects, packaging, hardware, storage, wear/repair and material clues that downstream artists can reuse without inventing era shorthand.
At least two ordinary task/use states showing where waiting, access, weather, movement, maintenance or system friction appears in daily life.
Research/source labels, authority status and OPEN fields stay visible so an attractive board cannot silently freeze unresolved year/place/incident/household details.

populationHousehold.purpose: Show era/generation/household diversity as production reference without defining the Core5 character's literal family.

requiredPanels.role: A comparable six-lens lineup/reference field for child, teen-or-young-adult, parent-age adult, older adult, non-parent aunt/uncle-like adult and one non-nuclear household example.
At least three non-identical household/access situations showing that one household type does not represent the era.
Show cooking/provisioning, work/study, care, repair, communication, travel or record-keeping distributed across roles without gender/age stereotype shorthand.
Compare access to devices, money/payment, transport, food/provisioning, records/privacy or maintenance across generations/households as appropriate to that era.

A visible production note stating that population lenses are research/reference composites and do not define the Core5 character's exact parents, siblings, grandparents, children, partner, address or household.

visualReadabilityRules: The main panel must be legible as a setting reference at overview scale while detail panels remain inspectable at zoom.
Labels must identify whether an element is EXISTING_CANON, RESEARCH_BACKED_CURRENT, AUTHOR_CANDIDATE or OPEN where ambiguity matters.
No panel may use beauty lighting, depth of field, weather or effects to hide system construction, material, signage or ordinary-use evidence.
Era-specific clutter must be functional evidence; decorative density is not historical authenticity.
Population silhouettes and props must preserve enough negative space to compare body/role/access differences without forced touching or visual merger.
A future board must look functionally plausible before it looks futuristic; present/historical boards must look lived-in before nostalgic.
